# AGENTS.md

## Development Commands

### Build
- `make build` - Build both frps and frpc binaries
- `make frps` - Build server binary only
- `make frpc` - Build client binary only
- `make all` - Build everything with formatting

### Testing
- `make test` - Run unit tests
- `make e2e` - Run end-to-end tests
- `make e2e-trace` - Run e2e tests with trace logging
- `make alltest` - Run all tests including vet, unit tests, and e2e

### Code Quality
- `make fmt` - Run go fmt
- `make fmt-more` - Run gofumpt for more strict formatting
- `make gci` - Run gci import organizer
- `make vet` - Run go vet
- `golangci-lint run` - Run comprehensive linting (configured in .golangci.yml)

### Assets
- `make web` - Build web dashboards (frps and frpc)

### Cleanup
- `make clean` - Remove built binaries and temporary files

## Testing

- E2E tests using Ginkgo/Gomega framework
- Mock servers in `/test/e2e/mock/`
- Run: `make e2e` or `make alltest`

- `doc/agents/release.md` - Release process

report.overview: frp is a fast reverse proxy written in Go that exposes services behind NATs/firewalls via a public server (frps) and an in-NAT client (frpc). It supports TCP, UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, TCPMUX, and secret/P2P modes (stcp, sudp, xtcp) over TCP, KCP, QUIC, WebSocket, or TLS control transports, with token/OIDC auth, HTTP-based server plugins, embedded Vue dashboards, and optional dynamic proxy persistence. The codebase is split into cmd/ entrypoints, server/ and client/ runtimes, and a large pkg/ shared library (config v1, msg protocol, wire v2, auth, nathole, plugins, vnet).

system_map.summary: The repo builds two binaries from a single Go module: frps (server, cmd/frps) and frpc (client, cmd/frpc), both driven by cobra. server/service.go constructs a Service that multiplexes control-plane listeners (TCP mux, KCP, QUIC, WebSocket, raw TLS, internal SSH pipe) on shared ports and owns the ControlManager, proxy.Manager, plugin.Manager, ports.Manager and vhost routers. client/service.go constructs a Service that dials frps through a pluggable Connector and keeps a Control session alive with backoff retries. Shared protocol and config code lives under pkg/ (msg, proto/wire, config/v1, auth, transport, util). State is entirely in-memory except an optional client-side JSON store for dynamic proxies. Two Vue 3 apps under web/ provide dashboards and are embedded via the assets package, or excluded with the 'noweb' build tag.

claims.claim: frps entrypoint is cmd/frps/root.go: cobra rootCmd.RunE loads config via config.LoadServerConfig, validates with validation.NewConfigValidator, then calls runServer -> server.NewService -> svr.Run.

frpc entrypoint is cmd/frpc/sub/root.go: runClient -> config.LoadClientConfigResult -> source.NewAggregator -> client.NewService -> svr.Run; a --config_dir flag runs one Service per file via runMultipleClients.

server.Service multiplexes the bind port with golib mux.Mux: default listener for TCP control, a prefix-matched websocket listener ('GET /~frp'), and a TLS listener that sniffs first byte 0x16 / FRPTLSHeadByte.

Optional listeners are created for KCP (netpkg.ListenKcp on KCPBindPort), QUIC (quic.ListenAddr with ALPN 'frp'), SSH tunnel gateway (ssh.NewGateway), and a tcpmux HTTPConnect multiplexer on TCPMuxHTTPConnectPort.
The wire protocol has two versions: acceptConnection calls wire.CheckMagic to detect v2, then negotiates crypto/UDP-codec via ClientHello/ServerHello frames before reading the first msg.

The client dials frps through a Connector interface (client/connector.go) supporting tcp, kcp, quic (one quic.Conn, streams converted via QuicStreamToNetConn), websocket/wss, and tls; ServiceOptions.ConnectorCreator allows swapping in a virtual pipe connector.

Server state is in-memory: registry.ClientRegistry tracks logical clients by user.clientID, proxy.Manager tracks live proxies, ports.Manager allocates TCP/UDP remote ports honoring AllowPorts, and vhost.Routers route HTTP(S) vhosts.
The only persistent state is the optional client-side StoreSource: a JSON file (store.path) holding dynamic proxies/visitors, merged with file config by source.Aggregator.
Dashboards are Vue 3 apps web/frps and web/frpc (npm workspaces under web/), embedded into Go via the assets package; Makefile adds a 'noweb' build tag when web/*/dist is absent.

Build produces CGO_ENABLED=0 binaries with build tags 'frps'/'frpc' plus optional 'noweb' (Makefile frps/frpc targets); go.mod pins go 1.25.0 with quic-go, kcp-go, yamux, gorilla/mux, go-oidc, prometheus, wireguard as key deps.
server/http and client/http packages implement admin API controllers behind gorilla/mux routers registered by registerRouteHandlers on each Service's webServer (httppkg.Server).
Both services disable quic-go receive-buffer warnings and ECN via env vars in package init, and set crypto.DefaultSalt = 'frp' for golib crypto.

feature_catalog.summary: frp exposes eight proxy types (tcp, udp, http, https, tcpmux, stcp, sudp, xtcp) plus three visitor types (stcp, sudp, xtcp) for private/P2P access. Features include token and OIDC auth, per-proxy encryption/compression/bandwidth limits, load-balancer groups, health checks, PROXY protocol and host-header rewriting, HTTP server plugins, client plugins (static_file, unix_domain_socket, http(s) converters, socks5, tls2raw, virtual_net), NAT hole punching via STUN, an SSH tunnel gateway, a WireGuard-based VirtualNet, Prometheus metrics, dashboards for both daemons, and a rich frpc CLI with per-type subcommands, verify, nathole discover and admin commands.

claims.claim: Eight proxy types are defined by proxyConfigTypeMap in pkg/config/v1/proxy.go (TCP, UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, TCPMUX, STCP, XTCP, SUDP); NewProxyConfigurerByType instantiates typed configurers via reflection.

frpc auto-generates a cobra subcommand per proxy type (tcp, udp, tcpmux, http, https, stcp, sudp, xtcp) plus visitor subcommands for stcp/sudp/xtcp, wiring flags via config.RegisterClientCommonConfigFlags/RegisterProxyFlags.
Auth supports token and OIDC methods: NewAuthSetter picks NewTokenAuth or Oidc setters/verifiers, and TokenSource can dynamically resolve tokens (file/exec) via Resolve.

Client-side plugins registered via init() include static_file, unix_domain_socket, http2http, http2https, https2http, https2https, socks5, tls2raw, virtual_net, and http_proxy; each registers a CreatorFn into pkg/plugin/client's creators map.

Server manage plugins are HTTP webhooks configured via HTTPPlugins; plugin.Manager supports six ops (Login, NewProxy, CloseProxy, Ping, NewWorkConn, NewUserConn) that can reject or mutate request content.

xtcp P2P mode uses NAT hole punching: client/visitor exchange NatHoleVisitor/NatHoleClient messages through frps' nathole.Controller, with STUN discovery defaulting to stun.easyvoip.com:3478 (natHoleStunServer).
stcp/sudp 'secret' proxies require a shared secretKey; visitors bind a local port and connect through frps visitor-manager admission (admitVisitorByRunID / visitor.Manager).
Load balancing groups exist for TCP (TCPGroupCtl), HTTP (HTTPGroupCtl), HTTPS and TCPMux, letting multiple proxies share a group key and remote port.
SSH tunnel gateway (SSHTunnelGateway.BindPort) accepts native ssh connections and forwards them into frps via an InternalListener handled like regular frp connections.

VirtualNet creates a TUN device (water + wireguard-go) so visitors get an IP on a virtual network; enabled via featureGates.VirtualNet and virtualNet.address, and cannot be enabled by hot reload alone.

frps dashboard API exposes /healthz, /api/serverinfo, /api/proxy/{type}[/{name}], /api/traffic/{name}, /api/clients, DELETE /api/proxies, plus a parallel /api/v2 surface (users, system/info, system/prune, clients, proxies) and /metrics when EnablePrometheus.
frpc admin API exposes /api/reload, /api/stop, /api/status, GET/PUT /api/config, per-proxy/visitor config reads, and CRUD under /api/store/proxies|visitors when the store source is enabled.
frpc CLI extras: 'verify' subcommand validates auth against a server, 'nathole discover' probes NAT behavior, and admin subcommands call the admin API.

Per-proxy transport features include useEncryption/useCompression (golib io wrappers), bandwidthLimit with client/server mode (rate.Limiter), and proxyProtocolVersion headers built by BuildProxyProtocolHeaderStruct.
Health checking of local services lives in client/health, and event hooks in client/event let proxies react to lifecycle events.

data_flow.summary: Config enters as TOML/YAML/JSON (or deprecated INI), is template-rendered with environment variables, decoded into pkg/config/v1 types, completed, and validated before use. Control-plane data flows as typed msg structs (Login, NewProxy, NewWorkConn, Ping, NatHole*) over a single muxed connection, versioned by the v1/v2 wire protocol. User traffic flows: public listener on frps -> proxy -> pooled work connection -> frpc -> optional plugin -> local service, joined byte streams via libio.Join. Admin data flows through gorilla/mux routers into adminapi controllers, and reloads re-merge config via the source.Aggregator.

claims.claim: Config loading: LoadFileContentWithTemplate renders Go templates exposing .Envs plus parseNumberRange helpers, then LoadConfigure tries TOML->JSON marshal, JSON detection via yaml.IsJSONBuffer, or YAML (with dot-field stripping), honoring strict mode.
Legacy INI configs are detected by a 'common' section and converted through pkg/config/legacy converters (Convert_ServerCommonConf_To_v1, Convert_ClientCommonConf_To_v1) before joining the v1 path.

Client proxy/visitor configs come from inline [[proxies]]/[[visitors]] plus includeConfigFiles globs (LoadAdditionalClientConfigs), dedup-checked by validateNoDuplicateNames, filtered by common.Start and enabled flags in FilterClientConfigurers.

Login handshake: client sends msg.Login over the control conn; server runs pluginManager.Login hooks, wraps the conn in an encrypted ReadWriter (AEAD for v2, crypto RW for v1), then RegisterControl admits and activates the Control, replying LoginResp{RunID}.

Proxy registration: client pm.UpdateAll sends msg.NewProxy; server handleNewProxy runs NewProxy plugin hooks, builds a configurer via config.NewProxyConfigurerFromMsg, creates a Proxy through proxyFactoryRegistry, runs it (acquiring ports/vhost routes) and answers NewProxyResp.

Work connections are pooled: server keeps workConnCh buffered at poolCount+10, sends msg.ReqWorkConn on demand; client handleReqWorkConn dials a fresh conn, writes authenticated NewWorkConn, waits for StartWorkConn, then hands the conn to the owning proxy.

TCP user traffic path on frpc: BaseProxy.InWorkConn -> HandleTCPWorkConnection -> wrapWorkConn (limiter -> encryption -> compression) -> optional proxyPlugin.Handle or dial localIP:localPort -> libio.Join(localConn, remote).

HTTP(S) traffic is routed by hostname through vhost.Routers into the matching proxy; frps can share the bind port with vhost ports by muxing HTTP/HTTPS listeners off mux.Mux when BindPort == VhostHTTP(S)Port.
UDP traffic uses msg.UDPPacket frames; the negotiated codec (udpPacketCodec) is fixed per session via the v2 ServerHello and passed into proxy/visitor managers.

Hot reload path: /api/reload -> apiController.Reload -> Service.UpdateConfigSource -> configSource.ReplaceAll -> reloadConfigFromSourcesLocked -> aggregator.Load -> Filter/Complete -> UpdateAllConfigurer -> ctl.pm/vm.UpdateAll.

Metrics flow: server/metrics.Server records NewClient/NewProxy/CloseProxy events during Control lifecycle; pkg/metrics EnableMem/EnablePrometheus are activated when webServer.Port > 0 and exposed at /metrics.

NatHole orchestration: NatHoleVisitor/NatHoleClient/NatHoleReport messages are dispatched as async handlers on the server Control and routed to nathole.Controller, which analyzes NAT behavior and replies NatHoleResp to visitors.

behavior_traces.summary: Four flows were traced end-to-end. (1) frps startup: cobra -> LoadServerConfig -> validate -> NewService wires all listeners/managers -> Run spawns per-listener goroutines. (2) frpc startup+login: cobra -> LoadClientConfigResult -> aggregator merge -> NewService -> Run -> loopLoginUntilSuccess -> controlSessionDialer.Dial -> NewControl -> ctl.Run. (3) TCP proxy request path: TCPProxy.Run listens -> user conn -> GetWorkConn -> ReqWorkConn -> client NewWorkConn -> StartWorkConn -> InWorkConn -> join to local service. (4) Admin reload: GET /api/reload -> Reload -> UpdateConfigSource -> reloadConfigFromSourcesLocked -> UpdateAllConfigurer.

claims.claim: frps startup order: rootCmd.RunE -> config.LoadServerConfig (legacy INI detection -> template render -> decode -> Complete) -> security.NewUnsafeFeatures + ValidateServerConfig -> runServer -> log.InitLogger -> server.NewService -> svr.Run.

server.NewService order: build TLS config -> optional webServer (+metrics) -> BuildServerAuth -> construct managers (ctlManager, pxyManager, pluginManager, ResourceController with port managers) -> register HTTP plugins -> group controllers -> bind muxed TCP listener -> optional KCP/QUIC/SSH/vhost listeners -> NatHoleController.

svr.Run spawns goroutines: webServer.Run, HandleListener(sshTunnelListener internal=true), HandleListener(kcp), HandleQUICListener, HandleListener(websocket), HandleListener(tls), NatHoleController.CleanWorker, sshTunnelGateway.Run, then blocks in HandleListener(main listener).

Inbound conn handling: HandleListener -> handleConnection -> acceptConnection (CheckMagic v1/v2, ClientHello negotiation, read first msg) -> switch on msg.Login/msg.NewWorkConn/msg.NewVisitorConn -> RegisterControl / RegisterWorkConn / RegisterVisitorConn.

Control lifecycle is generation-guarded: ControlManager.Add installs ctl as pending generation keyed by runID (replacing the old control and inheriting its runMu), Activate registers user.clientID in ClientRegistry (conflict -> error), completeLogin writes LoginResp then startLocked flips state to running and launches ctl.worker.

frpc startup order: runClient -> LoadClientConfigResult -> NewConfigSource.ReplaceAll -> optional NewStoreSource -> NewAggregator.Load -> Filter/Complete configurers -> ValidateAllClientConfig -> startServiceWithAggregator -> client.NewService -> svr.Run.

client.Service.Run order: optional DNSServer override -> vnetController.Init/Run -> admin webServer -> loopLoginUntilSuccess (first login failure can exit when loginFailExit) -> keepControllerWorking reconnection loop with FastBackoff (3 fast retries/min then exponential to 20s).

Client login + proxy bring-up: loopLoginUntilSuccess -> controlSessionDialer.Dial(runID) -> NewControl -> ctl.SetInWorkConnCallback -> ctl.Run -> pm.UpdateAll(proxyCfgs) sends NewProxy per proxy and vm.UpdateAll(visitorCfgs); worker starts heartbeatWorker and msgDispatcher.

Work conn establishment on demand: server GetWorkConn drains pool else sends ReqWorkConn and waits up to UserConnTimeout; client handleReqWorkConn -> connectServer -> authenticated NewWorkConn -> server RegisterWorkConn pushes into workConnCh -> proxy.Start writes StartWorkConn back to client.

TCP data path completion: client receives StartWorkConn -> pm.HandleWorkConn(proxyName) -> Proxy.InWorkConn -> HandleTCPWorkConnection wraps conn (limit/encrypt/compress) -> writes PROXY protocol header if configured -> dials localIP:localPort -> libio.Join for bidirectional copy.

Heartbeat: client heartbeatWorker sends authenticated msg.Ping every HeartbeatInterval with backoff and closes session when lastPong exceeds HeartbeatTimeout; server heartbeatWorker closes the Control when lastPing exceeds Transport.HeartbeatTimeout.

Admin reload trace: GET /api/reload -> apiController.Reload -> Service.UpdateConfigSource (reloadMu serialized) -> cfgSource.ReplaceAll -> reloadConfigFromSourcesLocked -> aggregator.Load -> VirtualNet requirement check -> UpdateAllConfigurer -> ctl.vm.UpdateAll + ctl.pm.UpdateAll.

testing_signals.summary: Unit tests use Go's testing with testify and rodaine/table, spread through pkg/, client/, server/ and cmd/ (run via `make test`/`gotest` with the noweb tag). End-to-end tests use Ginkgo/Gomega under test/e2e with a framework that spawns real frps/frpc binaries, organized into v1/basic, v1/features, plugin, legacy and mock server helpers; `make e2e` runs hack/run-e2e.sh with 16-way parallelism. Cross-version compatibility suites run released binaries via hack/run-e2e-compatibility.sh and download scripts. The web workspace uses Vitest + @vue/test-utils; linting is via golangci-lint (.golangci.yml) plus gofmt/gofumpt/gci/vet make targets and GitHub Actions workflows.

claims.claim: make gotest runs `go test -tags noweb -v --cover` over ./assets/..., ./cmd/..., ./client/..., ./server/..., ./pkg/...; make alltest adds vet and e2e.

E2E harness: test/e2e/e2e.go RunE2ETests registers Gomega fail handler, enables EmitSpecProgress and RandomizeAllSpecs; hack/run-e2e.sh installs ginkgo v2.23.4 and runs against bin/frpc and bin/frps (overridable via FRPC_PATH/FRPS_PATH).
E2E framework provides process management, port allocation, mock servers and request helpers under test/e2e/framework and test/e2e/pkg (cert, plugin, port, process, relay, request, rpc, ssh).

E2E coverage areas include basic client/server behavior, config, HTTP, tcpmux, xtcp, OIDC, token_source, wire protocol, plus features: bandwidth_limit, chaos, control_replacement, group, heartbeat, monitor, real_ip, ssh_tunnel, store.

Compatibility testing: make e2e-compatibility runs hack/run-e2e-compatibility.sh against FRP_COMPAT_BASELINE_COUNT released versions (floor 0.61.0); e2e-compatibility-last-frpc/last-frps download the last release into ./lastversion and run the suite with one side pinned old.

Unit tests exist for config decode/load (pkg/config/v1 *_test.go, pkg/config/load_test.go), msg codecs (pkg/msg msg_test.go, wire_v2_test.go, udp_binary_test.go + benchmarks), auth OIDC (pkg/auth/oidc_test.go), source aggregator/store, client service/config_manager/control_session, server control/service/proxy, nathole analysis/discovery, vnet controller, health.
cmd/frpc/sub has verify_test.go covering the verify subcommand; most other cmd code (proxy/admin/nathole subcommands) has no direct unit tests.

Web frontend testing: web/package.json defines test:unit via vitest run (vitest 4.1.10, jsdom, @vue/test-utils) across workspaces shared/frpc/frps; Makefile web-ci runs npm ci, lint:check, test:unit and builds.

Lint/format toolchain: golangci-lint run configured by .golangci.yml; make fmt (go fmt), fmt-more (gofumpt), gci (import grouping with frp prefix), vet; CI workflows include golangci-lint.yml and goreleaser.yml.
runMultipleClients (--config_dir) is explicitly documented as 'only designed for testing. It's not guaranteed to be stable' yet is reachable via a public flag.
Ginkgo parallel runs default to CONCURRENCY=16 in run-e2e.sh and framework.RunID isolates per-node resources.

risk_map.summary: The highest-risk areas are command-execution token sources (gated behind the TokenSourceExec unsafe feature), filesystem-serving and socket-exposing client plugins (static_file, unix_domain_socket which can expose docker.sock), the VirtualNet TUN setup that shells out to ifconfig/route on macOS, and admin web servers that depend on auth middleware correctness. Concurrency risk concentrates in server/control.go's ControlManager, which enforces a documented lock order (runMu -> cm.mu -> lifecycleMu -> registry) and generation handoff barriers; regressions there cause deadlocks or leaked controls. The deprecated INI path (pkg/config/legacy) and the testing-only --config_dir mode are legacy surface. Plugin content mutation uses a deliberate panic on wrong types.

claims.claim: ExecSource.Resolve executes arbitrary commands (exec.CommandContext with env passthrough) to produce auth tokens; it is gated by the TokenSourceExec entry in both ClientUnsafeFeatures and ServerUnsafeFeatures requiring --allow-unsafe.
VirtualNet setup on Darwin shells out to ifconfig and route to configure the TUN device; tun_linux.go uses netlink. Errors here are runtime-privilege dependent.
unix_domain_socket and static_file client plugins expose local filesystem paths/sockets remotely; README documents exposing /var/run/docker.sock as a TCP proxy, an intentionally dangerous capability.

Admin APIs (client /api/config PUT, /api/stop, /api/store/*; server DELETE /api/proxies, /api/v2/system/prune) are powerful mutation endpoints guarded only by helper.AuthMiddleware on the dashboard port — misconfiguration of webServer auth exposes full control.

ControlManager implements a strict multi-lock protocol (never wait on runMu holding cm.mu; order runMu -> cm.mu -> ctl.lifecycleMu -> registry locks) with generation IDs and handoff barriers; the complexity concentrates deadlock/race risk in control.go.
GetWorkConn recovers from panics and the worker teardown closes pooled conns, but a full workConnCh silently discards registered work conns ('work connection pool is full, discarding').

Plugin content mutation in handleMutableContent does retContent.(*T) with a comment 'Buggy Plugin implementations still panic here, by design' — a malicious/broken server plugin path can panic the handler goroutine.

Server plugins make outbound HTTP calls to user-configured addresses during login/proxy/workconn events; a plugin failure rejects the operation (errors fail closed for mutable ops like Login/NewProxy).

Legacy INI support is deprecated and routed through pkg/config/legacy converters; conf/legacy holds reference INI files. New features are TOML/YAML/JSON-only, so the legacy path is dead-end code that still runs when a 'common' section is detected.
xtcp relies on public STUN (default stun.easyvoip.com:3478) and NAT-behavior heuristics in nathole; P2P may silently fail on incompatible NATs — README itself recommends stcp fallback.
SSH tunnel gateway accepts native SSH connections on a dedicated port and pipes them into the control plane (InternalListener); it expands the server's attack surface to the SSH protocol.

Duplicate proxy/visitor names across merged config sources are rejected at load by validateNoDuplicateNames; before this check a duplicate would have been silently dropped — indicates historically fragile merge semantics.
frpc tlsListener sniffs first bytes to distinguish frp TLS from HTTPS; misclassification risk exists when vhostHTTPS shares the bind port (comment notes 0x16 ambiguity).

extension_points.summary: frp is built around registries. New proxy types plug in through three coordinated tables: proxyConfigTypeMap in pkg/config/v1, server-side RegisterProxyFactory (init() per type in server/proxy), and client-side RegisterProxyFactory (init() in client/proxy). Client connection-handling plugins register via pkg/plugin/client's Register/Create; server hooks come from external HTTP plugin processes managed by pkg/plugin/server. frpc CLI subcommands are generated automatically from the proxy type list. Config extensibility goes through source.Source implementations aggregated by source.Aggregator, and embedding is supported via pkg/virtual.Client plus ServiceOptions hooks (ConnectorCreator, HandleWorkConnCb). Feature gates (pkg/policy/featuregate) guard experimental features.

claims.claim: server/proxy uses a reflect.Type-keyed factory registry: each type file (tcp.go, udp.go, http.go, https.go, tcpmux.go, stcp.go, sudp.go, xtcp.go) calls RegisterProxyFactory in init(); adding a server proxy type means adding a config type + factory init.
client/proxy mirrors the pattern: RegisterProxyFactory keyed by configurer reflect.Type, invoked from NewProxy which first builds a BaseProxy with limiter/encryption key/msgTransporter.

Client plugins register a CreatorFn by name via plugin.Register (panics on duplicate) and are instantiated lazily in BaseProxy.Run when baseCfg.Plugin.Type is set; the Plugin interface is Handle(ctx, *ConnectionInfo) + Close.

Server plugin ops are an open enum: Manager.Register bins each Plugin by IsSupport(op) into per-op slices for Login, NewProxy, CloseProxy, Ping, NewWorkConn, NewUserConn; new ops require extending the manager dispatch.
frpc single-proxy subcommands are generated in a loop over proxyTypes, so a new type automatically gains a CLI command and (for stcp/sudp/xtcp) a nested visitor command.

Config sources are pluggable: source.Aggregator merges a ConfigSource (in-memory/file) with an optional StoreSource; Service consumes aggregator.Load() at boot and on reload, so new persistence backends slot in as Source implementations.

Embedding hooks: client.ServiceOptions exposes ConnectorCreator (custom transports/virtual clients) and HandleWorkConnCb (intercept work conns); pkg/virtual.Client demonstrates running frpc against an in-process InternalListener.
pkg/sdk/client provides a programmatic client API for running proxies from Go code rather than config files.

Admin routes are registered centrally in each Service's registerRouteHandlers, so new endpoints slot into the gorilla/mux subRouter (with auth middleware already applied); server has a separate encoded-path subrouter for /api/v2 names.
Feature gates: ClientCommonConfig.FeatureGates map plus pkg/policy/featuregate control rollout of features like VirtualNet; reload path validates gate-dependent config against runtime capabilities.
vhost.Routers + vhost.NewHTTPReverseProxy/NewHTTPSMuxer are the extension seam for HTTP(S) routing behavior; group controllers (TCP/HTTP/HTTPS/TCPMux) encapsulate shared-port load balancing.

Message/protocol extension: msg.Dispatcher.RegisterHandler maps message structs to handlers on both sides; adding a control message means defining it in pkg/msg and registering handlers in client/control.go and server/control.go.

agent_handoff.summary: Start with AGENTS.md for the command surface: `make build|frps|frpc|test|e2e|fmt|fmt-more|gci|vet`, `golangcici-lint run`, `make web`. Read cmd/frps/root.go + cmd/frpc/sub/root.go, then server/service.go and client/service.go for wiring, and server/control.go for the lifecycle/locking protocol before touching session code. Config changes must go through pkg/config/v1 types + validation and be tested for TOML/YAML/JSON and strict mode. Protocol changes must update pkg/msg on both sides and consider the v2 wire negotiation in pkg/proto/wire. E2E tests need built binaries and Ginkgo; unit tests run with the noweb tag when dashboards aren't built.

claims.claim: AGENTS.md documents the canonical commands: make build/frps/frpc/test/e2e/e2e-trace/alltest/fmt/fmt-more/gci/vet, make web for dashboards, and points to doc/agents/ runbooks (release.md).

First files to read: cmd/frps/root.go and cmd/frpc/sub/root.go (entrypoints), server/service.go and client/service.go (composition roots), server/control.go (session lifecycle/locking), pkg/config/v1 (config schema), pkg/msg/msg.go (protocol).
Build tags matter: 'frps'/'frpc' select per-binary code and 'noweb' is auto-added when web/*/dist is missing — run go test/vet with -tags noweb or build dashboards first.

When editing server/control.go, respect the documented global lock order (runMu, cm.mu, ctl.lifecycleMu, then registry locks) and the pending/activated/running state machine — generation handoff uses barriers between replaced controls.

Config edits require updating v1 types, Complete() defaults, validation.Validate* and ideally e2e coverage; strict_config=true by default rejects unknown fields, so new fields break older parsers cross-version.
Client config now flows through source.Aggregator (ConfigSource + StoreSource); bypassing it breaks /api/reload and store CRUD. Keep Service.reloadMu semantics when touching UpdateConfigSource.
Run `go test -tags noweb ./pkg/... ./client/... ./server/...` for unit tests; `make e2e` requires bin/frps+bin/frpc built first and ginkgo installed (script auto-installs).

Don't add proxy types piecemeal: a type needs a configurer in proxyConfigTypeMap, marshal/unmarshal to msg, server factory init, client factory init, validation, and usually e2e — the CLI subcommand is then auto-generated.
Auth token bytes double as the work-conn encryption key (ClientAuth/ServerAuth key = []byte(resolved.Token)) — changing token handling affects transport encryption.
Version pinning/compat is enforced by tests: FRP_COMPAT_FLOOR_VERSION=0.61.0 and baseline-count e2e runs mean wire/protocol changes must remain compatible across ~8 released versions.

Logging uses pkg/util/log and xlog (context-scoped, prefixed by runID); follow existing xl.Debugf/Tracef patterns rather than fmt.Println in service code (entrypoints print user-facing errors via fmt).
Panic-on-duplicate registries (plugin.Register, proxy factories) run in init() — import cycles or double registration crash at startup, so new plugins/types must use unique names/types.

report.agent_prompt:
You are working on frp (github.com/fatedier/frp), a Go reverse proxy that exposes services behind NATs. Two binaries share one module: frps (server, cmd/frps) and frpc (client, cmd/frpc). Read AGENTS.md first for commands: `make build` (or `make frps`/`make frpc`), `make test` (unit, uses -tags noweb), `make e2e` (Ginkgo suite in test/e2e, needs built binaries), `make fmt`/`gofumpt`/`gci`/`vet`, `golangci-lint run`, `make web` for the Vue dashboards.

Architecture: cmd/frps/root.go and cmd/frpc/sub/root.go parse config (TOML/YAML/JSON via pkg/config/load.go with Go-template env substitution; legacy INI auto-converted via pkg/config/legacy) and call server.NewService / client.NewService. server/service.go wires a muxed bind-port listener (TCP + websocket prefix + TLS sniff), optional KCP/QUIC/SSH/vhost listeners, ControlManager, proxy.Manager, ports.Manager, plugin.Manager and vhost routers. client/service.go dials frps via a pluggable Connector (tcp/kcp/quic/websocket/tls), logs in (msg.Login -> LoginResp{runID}), then runs a Control session that registers proxies (NewProxy) and fills a work-conn pool on ReqWorkConn. User traffic: server proxy listener -> pooled work conn -> StartWorkConn -> client proxy InWorkConn -> optional client plugin -> dial localIP:localPort -> libio.Join.

Key extension points: proxy types require coordinated changes — proxyConfigTypeMap in pkg/config/v1/proxy.go, server/proxy RegisterProxyFactory init, client/proxy RegisterProxyFactory init, msg marshal/unmarshal, validation; frpc subcommands auto-generate from the type list. Client plugins register in pkg/plugin/client (Register/Create); server plugins are external HTTP webhooks (pkg/plugin/server ops: Login, NewProxy, CloseProxy, Ping, NewWorkConn, NewUserConn). Config sources go through pkg/config/source.Aggregator (ConfigSource + optional JSON StoreSource backing /api/store/*).

Traps: server/control.go enforces a strict lock order (runMu -> cm.mu -> ctl.lifecycleMu -> registry) with control-generation barriers — read it before touching session lifecycle. The auth token is also the work-conn encryption key. ExecSource (auth token via subprocess) is gated behind --allow-unsafe TokenSourceExec. VirtualNet needs the feature gate at startup and shells out to ifconfig/route on macOS. E2E compatibility tests pin ~8 released versions (floor 0.61.0) — protocol changes must stay wire-compatible across v1/v2 negotiation in pkg/proto/wire. Config strict mode is on by default. When in doubt, mirror an existing proxy type (tcp) end-to-end.
